origins.description: This input defines the revised gate shape, sealed-binding contract and runner-lib clauses per the explicit user rulings recorded in decisions. Not historical truth.

legalDomain.toolBinding: One sealed binding per gate method, owned by the implementation side: script constant, timeout budget, argument encoding, result codec. The gate face never exposes script, process, or timeout vocabulary; callers pass business values only (SkuId or nothing).
legalDomain.probeProtocol: Exactly one line, no LF or CR. ANSWER|<sku>|<nonnegative Long> or REFUSED|<code>|<message>. Exact three-field arity; separator characters are structurally excluded by the arity check. The codec is the decode-side framing guard of the security chain.
legalDomain.refusalFields: code and message are nonempty; a refusal is a typed business result on the success channel, never a failure-channel conversion.
legalDomain.directoryProtocol: Exactly one line, no LF or CR. DIRECTORY|<warehouseId>|<loc1>,<loc2,...>; an empty tail decodes to the empty vector; a trailing location separator is malformed; repeated locations stay verbatim in declared order.
legalDomain.failureChannels: Transport failures, TimeoutViolation, ConcurrencyRejected, ScriptRejected and ProtocolViolation live on the Future failure channel; refusals and answers live on the success channel. No shape is ever synthesized from a failure.
legalDomain.runnerLib: LocalProcessRunner.run(request) performs exactly one bounded subprocess execution per call and yields one output line; the three contract clauses (argv-direct delivery, exclusive bounded lifecycle with kill, script-pinning hook) are the hardening seam. Concrete spawn/timeout/concurrency mechanics are handwritten in infrastructure.process and stay outside the gate's executable surface; the sandbox denies process-exec, so the gate verifies compile plus seam-contract doubles — never a live process. Deployment hardening tiers (bounded lib, pinned scripts, sandboxed spawn, daemon-client transport) swap at this one binding.
legalDomain.delegation: Exactly one runner call per gate call; ProcessRequest(script, argument, timeoutMs) passed through verbatim — the sealed script constant, the business value as a single argument element (sku.value), the sealed timeout; no retry, no exception swallowing, no synthesized success; ExecutionContext injected explicitly, used only for Future transformation.
legalDomain.assembly: infrastructure.bootstrap.StockCatalogModule binds the gate to the sample-support implementation with an explicit Guice binding; the kernel-facing face carries no implementation reference; the test seam module supplies runner and ExecutionContext instances.

decisions.choice: USER RULING 2026-11-19: the connector vocabulary is too large a name for a local-process tool face — generated vocabulary becomes toolgate (application.toolgates / infrastructure.toolgates, StockCatalogToolGate), the runner becomes LocalProcessRunner with ProcessRequest(script, argument, timeoutMs); registry family IDs (#13/#25) stay unchanged as the ledger of which raw artifacts are being migrated.

USER RULING 2026-11-19: gate methods take business parameters only; the raw scriptParam shape (caller picks the executed script) is rejected as a target form and recorded raw-only for generator observation fixtures. Tool scripts are sealed generation-time constants.

USER RULING 2026-11-19: the runner is a fixed handwritten lib (infrastructure.process outer domain), not a family artifact; its contract carries the three hardening clauses and named violations (TimeoutViolation, ConcurrencyRejected, ScriptRejected) on the failure channel; security upgrades bind at the runner seam alone. Divergence resolution of v1 D6: the runner copy moves to infrastructure.process in both families; the v1 bundle stays frozen as approved.

Runner ABI is run(ProcessRequest): Future[String]; parameterless gate methods pass the empty argument with their sealed binding; no live process inside the quality gate (sandbox denies process-exec) — coverage is compile plus seam-contract doubles, per the diff 11.3 honesty boundary.
USER RULING 2026-11-18 carried over: no @ImplementedBy — kernel isolation; assembly is the explicit infrastructure.bootstrap Guice binding.
Formatting carried from v1: short Future name, single alphabetically sorted import block per file; v2 adds the toolgates package moves.

Malformed payloads, illegal identifiers and non-single-line inputs always fail with a named ProtocolViolation on the failure channel; runner violations are named values, never thrown; nothing is silently defaulted, truncated or coerced.
